name: 黄绢祠
Yellow Silk Shrine
before: 山脚下一座小石祠，祠里没有神像，供着一只黄绸包袱，绣着一条褪了色的龙。漂客们拜了它十年，逢初一十五往前头摆椰子。一队亡弓守着祠门，谁跪下磕头都不管，可谁伸手去碰包袱，箭就钉在谁的手边。

A little stone shrine at the foot of the hills, with no idol inside, only a bundle of yellow silk embroidered with a faded dragon. The castaways have worshipped it for ten years, setting coconuts before it on the first and fifteenth of each month. A squad of dead archers guards the door. They don't mind who kneels and kowtows, but reach for the bundle and an arrow lands beside your hand.
after: 亡弓退了。墨三屏着气解开包袱：里头是一只空了的诏封，封口的火漆早已剖开，封面一行字：「密。付千里号船主沈渡，至归墟启。」诏书不在。漂客们听说拜了十年的是个空信封，面面相觑，又一齐跪下磕了个头：「空的也是皇上的。」

The archers withdraw. Mo San holds his breath and unties the bundle: inside is an empty edict cover, its wax seal long since slit, and on its face a line: 'Secret. To Shen Du, master of the Qianli. To be opened at the Ruins.' The edict itself is gone. Hearing that they have been worshipping an empty envelope for ten years, the castaways look at one another, then all kneel and kowtow once more. 'Empty or not, it's still the Emperor's.'

name: 让路营
Parted Camp
before: 野地里一座大营，三路守墟人扎得严严实实，亡兵在前，亡弓在两翼，亡骑在后。可营当中让开了一条笔直的道，宽一人，草被踩得倒向东边。营里的守墟人一见你们，那条道一下子合上了，枪尖齐齐转了过来。

A great camp in the open, Ruin-keepers drawn up tight in three columns: soldiers in front, archers on the wings, riders behind. Yet straight through the middle runs a lane one person wide, the grass trodden flat towards the east. The moment the keepers see you, the lane snaps shut and every spear point swings your way.
after: 守墟人退了。营边放羊的漂客说，昨天傍晚有个女人从西边来，白头发，腰上挂一把短刀，手里捧着一本账。守墟人一个个往两边让，她看都没看它们，从营当中走了过去，只问了他一句：「我的船呢？」阿舟望着那条倒伏的草：「是她。」

The keepers withdraw. Yesterday at dusk, says a castaway herding goats at the camp's edge, a woman came from the west, white-haired, a short knife at her belt and a ledger in her hands. The keepers stepped aside one by one, and she walked straight through the middle of the camp without a glance at them. She asked him only one thing: 'Where is my ship?' Azhou looks along the flattened grass. 'It's her.'

name: 学声垭
Echo Mimic Pass
before: 山脚下一道窄垭口，冲里头喊一声，回声不是你的话：喊「有人吗」，回来的是「没有」；喊「借过」，回来的是「不借」。一队亡兵守在垭口，被回声骂得直往后缩，又不肯走。卤妹扯着嗓子喊了声「你是真的还是假的」，垭口里回了一句：「你猜。」

A narrow pass at the foot of the hills where the echo never repeats what you said. Shout 'Anyone there?' and back comes 'No.' Shout 'Let us through' and back comes 'Won't.' A squad of dead soldiers guards the pass, cringing back under the echo's abuse but refusing to leave. Lu Mei yells, 'Are you real or fake?' and the pass answers: 'Guess.'
after: 亡兵退了，石缝里钻出个瘦老头，是他在学回声，专吓守墟人。他说那年千里号的人在黄绢祠开了诏，到这垭口里大声念了一遍，他躲在缝里听，字认不全，只记住最后一句：「凡三百行，末一行空，候后来者。」他学了十年回声，就这一句不敢学：「那不是我能替人答的。」

The soldiers fall back and a skinny old man squeezes out of a crack in the rock. It was him mimicking the echo, to frighten the keepers. That year, he says, the Qianli's people opened the edict at the Yellow Silk Shrine and came into this pass to read it aloud. He hid in the crack and listened. He couldn't follow every word, but he remembers the last line: 'Three hundred lines in all. The last left blank, for whoever comes after.' Ten years he's mimicked echoes, and that one line he has never dared repeat. 'That's not an answer I can give for anyone.'

name: 旱舟原
Dry Ship Plain
before: 离海十几里的野地上，端端正正坐着一条大船，船身完好，三根桅还立着，甲板上长满了草，船尾两个大字：「千里」。一队亡骑绕着船跑，不许人上去。船头的绳梯下站着一个白发女人，腰挂短刀，仰着头看了很久：沈渡。她没回头：「十年，我在蜃楼替它记路，它倒先上了岸。」

A dozen li from the sea, a great ship sits squarely upright in open country, hull whole, three masts still standing, grass grown thick over her deck, and two great characters on her stern: 'Qianli'. A troop of dead riders gallops round her and lets no one climb aboard. At the foot of the rope ladder by the bow stands a white-haired woman with a short knife at her belt, gazing up a long while: Shen Du. She doesn't turn. 'Ten years I kept her road in the Mirage, and she came ashore before me.'
after: 亡骑散了。老漂客说，那年远海底下地动，浪在深海里只有一尺来高，船上的人连觉都没惊醒；到了浅湾，水底一浅，浪就立起来几丈高，把泊着的一号船端上了岸，一路送到这里放下。沈渡掀开货舱：丝、茶、瓷，捆得好好的，贴着「回程货」，十年没人动过一根绳。漂客们围着船摆开了摊，石料换金属的买卖开了张。她走进船长舱，打开诏匣，匣里是空的。「名单不在船上，」她说，「他们带着往东去了，交给了等在那边的人。」

The riders scatter. That year, an old castaway says, the seabed quaked somewhere far out. In the deep sea the wave stood barely a foot high and nobody aboard any ship even woke; but in the shallow bay, where the bottom rose, it reared up several zhang and lifted Ship Number One off her moorings, carrying her overland and setting her down here. Shen Du opens the hold: silk, tea, porcelain, bound tight and labelled 'Homeward cargo', not a rope touched in ten years. The castaways set up stalls around the ship, and stone-for-metal trade opens. She goes into the master's cabin and opens the edict box. It is empty. 'The list isn't aboard,' she says. 'They took it east and gave it to whoever was waiting there.'

name: 刻甲滩
Carved Shell Beach
before: 海边一片白沙滩，夜里海龟一只只爬上来下蛋。一伙落难海盗守着沙滩，等龟下完蛋就扒窝，还要把母龟翻过来，背朝下，抬回去熬汤。漂客们拦不住，蹲在沙丘后面看，海龟翻在沙上，四只鳍慢慢地划，划不着地。

On a white beach on the coast, sea turtles crawl ashore one by one at night to lay. A band of shipwrecked pirates holds the beach, waiting for each turtle to finish so they can dig out the nest, then flipping the mother onto her back to carry off for soup. The castaways can't stop them and crouch behind the dunes watching, the overturned turtles slowly paddling their flippers at nothing.
after: 海盗被赶下了滩，你们把翻倒的海龟一只只翻了回去。有一只老龟背甲上刻着几个浅浅的字：「丁未·千里」。漂客们说，母龟认生它的那片滩，游得再远也回来下蛋。那几年千里号的人在小龟背上刻了字放进海里：「它们会回来，我们也会。」今年，回来了一只。

The pirates are driven off the beach and you turn the overturned turtles back one by one. One old turtle has a few faint characters carved into her shell: 'Dingwei. Qianli.' A mother turtle knows the beach she hatched on, the castaways say, and however far she swims she comes back there to lay. In those years the Qianli's people carved hatchlings' shells and let them into the sea. 'They'll come back, and so will we.' This year, one has come back.

name: 朔夜市
New Moon Market
before: 初一的夜里，没有月亮，野地上忽然摆开了一溜摊子，摊主全是守墟人：亡兵蹲着，亡骑牵着马，面前各摆一样小东西，一把梳子、一只顶针、半截烟杆。它们互相换，换了又换回来，一句话也没有。你们一走近，所有的摊子一齐收了，亡骑翻身上马冲了过来。

On the night of the new moon, with no moon at all, a row of stalls suddenly appears in the open, and every stallkeeper is a Ruin-keeper: soldiers squatting, riders holding their horses, each with one small thing set out in front of them: a comb, a thimble, half a pipe stem. They trade among themselves, then trade back, without a word. As you come near every stall packs up at once and the riders vault into the saddle and charge.
after: 守墟人散了，地上落下几样东西。墨三捡起那只顶针，内圈刻着「柳」；梳子背上刻着「刘一刀」。漂客们说，千里号的人往东走的前一夜，挨个给守墟人送了一样随身的东西：「看了我们这么多年，留个念想。」守墟人每到初一就拿出来换着看，像在一遍遍地数那些人。

The keepers scatter, leaving a few things on the ground. Mo San picks up the thimble: 'Liu' is engraved inside the rim; the comb's spine reads 'Liu One-Stroke'. The night before the Qianli's people went east, the castaways say, they gave each keeper something they carried. 'You watched us all these years. Something to remember us by.' Every new moon the keepers bring them out and trade them round, as if counting those people over and over.

name: 塑面坳
Clay Face Hollow
before: 五条路交会的山坳里，地上摆满了泥捏的人脸，有的捏了一半，有的鼻子歪到耳朵边。一队亡兵蹲在泥塘边，挖泥，捏，举到自己平平的脸前比一比，摇摇头，拍碎了重捏。你们一进坳，它们扔下泥巴，抄起枪围了上来。

In a hollow where five roads meet, the ground is covered with faces modelled in clay, some half done, some with the nose slid round by the ear. A squad of dead soldiers squats by a clay pit, digging, moulding, holding each face up before their own flat ones to compare, shaking their heads, smashing it and starting again. As you enter they drop the clay, snatch up their spears and close in.
after: 亡兵退了，坳里只剩一地泥脸。你们挑出几张捏得最好的：一张胖脸，一张眯眼的黑脸，一张笑出酒窝的小脸。阿汐拿起那张黑脸，愣了半天：眉眼粗得很，可那副眯着眼看海的神气，是她爹。守墟人捏的不是自己的脸，是那些走了的人的脸。

The soldiers withdraw, leaving a hollow full of clay faces. You pick out a few of the best: a fat face, a squinting dark face, a small face with dimpled cheeks. Axi picks up the dark one and stands staring: the features are crude, but that squint out to sea is her father's. The keepers were not trying to make their own faces. They were making the faces of the people who left.

name: 船长椅
The Captain's Chair
before: 野地里一座漂客的小村，村口晒谷场当中摆着一把高背椅，椅背雕着浪花，扶手磨得发亮，村长每天坐在上头断事。一队亡兵这几天轮着来坐那把椅子，坐下就不起来，村长只好蹲在旁边断事。沈渡站在场边看着那把椅子，看了很久，嘴角动了一下。

A little castaway village in the open, and in the middle of its threshing floor stands a high-backed chair, its back carved with waves, its arms worn glossy. The headman sits in it every day to settle disputes. For days now dead soldiers have taken turns sitting in it and refusing to get up, so the headman has had to squat beside it to do his judging. Shen Du stands at the edge of the floor looking at the chair a long while, and the corner of her mouth twitches.
after: 亡兵被请下了椅子，村长才说，这是从一号船上搬下来的，大浪之后在泥里捡的。沈渡坐上去，往后一靠，靠出一声叹气：「我在这把椅子上坐不了半个时辰，就被一只黄猫挤下去。」她问：「猫呢？」阿汐说猫在淡水岛，蹲在「后来者」的水桶上。沈渡笑了：「它倒比我先懂。」

The soldiers are coaxed out of the chair and the headman explains: it came off Ship Number One, dug out of the mud after the great wave. Shen Du sits down and leans back with a sigh. 'I could never sit in this chair half an hour before a yellow cat squeezed me out of it. Where's the cat?' On Freshwater Island, Axi tells her, sitting on a barrel marked 'For whoever comes after'. Shen Du laughs. 'Trust it to understand before I did.'

name: 东望口
East Gaze Gap
before: 大路到这里收成一道窄口，两边是礁石垒的矮墙，墙头一排守墟的亡弓，弓弦拉得满满的。窄口外头，野地往东微微隆起，隆起的地方有光，一点一点，像有人在那边点了一大片灯，静静的，不晃。沈渡在窄口前停下了脚：「就是那儿。」

Here the main road narrows to a gap between low walls of piled reef stone, a line of dead archers on top with their bows at full draw. Beyond the gap the open land swells gently to the east, and on the swell there is light, point after point, as though someone has lit a great field of lamps over there, still and unflickering. Shen Du stops before the gap. 'That's the place.'
after: 亡弓退了，窄口开了。墙脚下压着一块木牌，是许潮生的字：「船主未至。名单交守灯人。」沈渡把木牌拿在手里翻了两遍，没说话。阿汐数着远处的灯，数到一半就数乱了。小桨趴在地上听了一会儿：「那边没有人声，可是有人在走，一个人，走得很慢。」

The archers withdraw and the gap opens. Pinned under the wall is a wooden board in Xu Chaosheng's hand: 'The master has not come. The list is given to the lamp keeper.' Shen Du turns it over twice in her hands and says nothing. Axi tries to count the distant lights and loses count halfway. Xiaojiang lies with his ear to the ground a while. 'No voices over there. But someone's walking. One person, walking very slowly.'

name: 押归坊
Homecoming Bet House
before: 野地里一座大棚，是落难海盗开的赌坊，赌的只有一样：千里号的人哪天回来。墙上贴满了押条，押初一的、押十五的、押明年的，十年里没有一张赢过。一大伙海盗守着赌坊，三路排开，见了你们的灯笼，庄家一拍桌子：「来押的还是来砸的？」

A great shed in the open, a gambling house run by shipwrecked pirates, and only one thing is bet on: the day the Qianli's people come back. The walls are papered with betting slips, on the first of the month, the fifteenth, next year; in ten years not one has won. A large crowd of pirates guards the place in three columns, and when they see your lanterns the banker slaps the table. 'Here to bet, or here to smash the place?'
after: 海盗被打散，庄家抱着钱匣子求饶。押条堆里只有一张没押日子，写着「不回来，往前走」，押的是一文钱，落款是漂客家的一个孩子。庄家苦笑：「十年了，就这一张一直没输。」墨三把那张押条揭下来，夹进了自己的簿子。

The pirates are scattered and the banker clutches his cash box, begging for mercy. In the heap of slips only one names no day at all. It reads 'They won't come back, they'll go on ahead', the stake is a single copper, and it is signed by a castaway child. The banker smiles wryly. 'Ten years, and that's the only slip that's never lost.' Mo San peels it off the wall and tucks it into his book.

name: 归墟眼
Eye of the Ruins
before: 海边一道小湾，湾里的静水冒着白汽，一串串气泡从水底往上翻，礁石结着一层黄壳，一股臭鸡蛋味。漂客们管这里叫归墟眼，说天下的水都从这儿漏下去，掉进去的人就到了海底下的另一个世界。一队亡兵站在冒汽的水里，水没到胸口，守着湾口不许人靠近。

A small cove on the coast where the still water steams, strings of bubbles rolling up from the bottom, the rocks crusted yellow, and a smell of rotten eggs. The castaways call it the Eye of the Ruins: all the world's water drains away down here, they say, and whoever falls in arrives in another world beneath the sea. A squad of dead soldiers stands chest-deep in the steaming water, barring the cove.
after: 亡兵退了，卤妹蹲下摸了摸水，烫手。她敲下一块黄壳舔了舔，呸了一口：「是硫黄。水不是往下漏，是往上冒的。」海水渗进底下旧火山的热石头里，烧热了，带着硫黄又翻上来。归墟不是天下的水归去的地方，是地底下冒热水的地方。龚墨斗挠头：「那叫『归墟』，岂不是叫反了？」

The soldiers withdraw and Lu Mei crouches to touch the water: hot enough to scald. She knocks off a flake of the yellow crust, licks it and spits. 'Sulphur. The water isn't draining down, it's coming up.' Seawater seeps down into the hot rock of the old volcano below, heats up, and wells back out carrying sulphur. Everyone says the Ruins are where all the world's water returns to; in truth it is where hot water pours out from under the earth. Gong Modou scratches his head. 'Then calling it the Return Ruins has it backwards.'

name: 牵星台
Star Board Platform
before: 野地里一座石台，台面上刻满了横道，一道挨一道，像一把大尺子。台边立着一根木柱，柱上挂着十几块大小不一的乌木板。一队亡弓占着石台，夜夜朝天放箭，射一箭，抬头看一会儿，像在射星星，射了不知多少年。

A stone platform in the open, its top scored with line after line like a giant ruler. Beside it stands a wooden post hung with a dozen ebony boards of different sizes. A squad of dead archers has taken the platform and shoots at the sky every night, loosing an arrow, then gazing upward for a while, as if shooting at the stars. They have been at it for who knows how many years.
after: 亡弓退了，阿汐取下一块乌木板，伸直胳膊对着北边的天一比：「是牵星板。」下沿齐海面，上沿齐北辰，量出北辰几指高，就知道船在南北哪一线上。台上的刻道是爹和鲍老针一夜夜量下来的，最后一行：「北辰高三指一角。往东，守此线。」他们往东走，一直守着这一指的高低。

The archers withdraw and Axi takes down an ebony board, holds it at arm's length against the northern sky. 'Star boards.' Line the bottom edge with the sea and the top with the Pole Star; whichever board fits tells you how many fingers high the Pole Star stands, and that tells you which line north or south your ship is on. The marks on the platform were measured night after night by her father and Bao Laozhen. The last line reads: 'Pole Star three fingers and a quarter. Going east, hold this line.' Wherever they went east, they kept the Pole Star at that one height.

name: 拜东坪
Eastward Bow Flat
before: 野地里一片平坪，每天日出，一大营守墟人在坪上排成一行行，亡兵、亡弓、亡骑，一齐朝东弯腰，弯下去就不起来，直到太阳升过一竿高。坪上的漂客也跟着拜，拜了十年，没人知道拜的是什么。你们一上坪，守墟人直起腰，转过身来。

A level flat in the open. Every sunrise a great camp of Ruin-keepers lines up on it rank on rank, soldiers, archers and riders, and bows to the east together, staying bent until the sun is a pole's height up. The castaways on the flat bow with them; they have done it for ten years and no one knows what they are bowing to. As you step onto the flat the keepers straighten and turn round.
after: 守墟人退了，坪上的老漂客才说起头一回：那天清早，千里号的人在这坪上排成行，朝守墟人鞠了一躬，谢它们看了这么多年，然后转身往东走了。守墟人站着没动，等人走远了，才学着弯下腰。「它们不是拜东边，」老人说，「是在回那个礼，回了十年，还没回完。」

The keepers withdraw, and only then does an old castaway tell how it began. Early one morning the Qianli's people lined up on this flat and bowed to the keepers, thanking them for watching over them all those years, then turned and walked east. The keepers stood without moving, and only when the people were far away did they bend down in imitation. 'They're not bowing to the east,' the old man says. 'They're returning that bow. Ten years they've been returning it and they're not done yet.'

name: 搬货道
Porters' Track
before: 野地里一条踩得发亮的土道，一大队守墟人排成长串，一个接一个地扛着木箱往东走，亡兵扛，亡弓背，亡骑驮在马上。箱子上烙着「千里」两个字，是从一号船上搬下来的。走到道尽头，它们放下箱子，又空着手往回走，再扛下一箱。

A track trodden shiny across the open land, and a great column of Ruin-keepers files along it carrying wooden crates east, soldiers shouldering them, archers with them on their backs, riders with them slung across their horses. The crates are branded 'Qianli': cargo off Ship Number One. At the track's end they set the crates down, walk back empty-handed, and fetch the next.
after: 守墟人退了，道尽头码着几十只木箱，码得方方正正。沈渡打开一只：是灯油，一罐一罐，封着蜡。她数了数，又看了看东边的光，脸色变了一下：「一号船上的灯油，够点二百九十九盏灯点十年。有人一直在拿。」她把箱子盖上：「不是守墟人要的，是有人教它们搬的。」

The keepers withdraw, leaving dozens of crates stacked square at the track's end. Shen Du opens one: lamp oil, jar after jar, sealed with wax. She counts, looks at the lights to the east, and something crosses her face. 'There was enough lamp oil on Number One to keep two hundred and ninety-nine lamps burning ten years. Someone has been taking it all this time.' She closes the lid. 'The keepers didn't want it. Someone taught them to carry it.'

name: 放鸢坡
Kite Slope
before: 野地里一道长坡，坡顶插着一排竹竿，竿上缠着断了的风筝线。漂客们说，每年八月十八，他们都在这儿放风筝，往东放，风筝上写着千里号的人名。可归墟没有风，风筝飞不起来，他们就举着风筝往东跑。今年一队守墟人占了坡顶，把风筝一只只扯碎。

A long slope in the open, a row of bamboo poles along its crest wound with broken kite strings. Every year on the eighteenth of the eighth month, the castaways say, they fly kites here, towards the east, with the Qianli's names written on them. But the Ruins have no wind and the kites won't rise, so they hold them up and run east with them. This year a band of Ruin-keepers has taken the crest and is tearing the kites to pieces one by one.
after: 守墟人被赶下坡，孩子们捡起没扯碎的风筝，举着往东跑，跑到坡底，风筝还是贴着地。墨三看着那些风筝上的名字，一个个对过：许潮生、鲍老针、老鼎、柳娘子……对到最后一只，风筝上什么也没写。孩子说：「这只是给不知道名字的那个人的。」

The keepers are driven off the slope and the children gather the kites still whole and run east holding them up. They reach the bottom with the kites still skimming the ground. Mo San checks the names on them one by one: Xu Chaosheng, Bao Laozhen, Old Ding, Doctor Liu... The last kite has nothing written on it at all. 'That one's for the one whose name nobody knows,' a child says.

name: 石舫岸
Stone Boat Shore
before: 海边岸上搁着一条船，是石头砌的，船头船尾、舷墙桅座，一样不缺，就是不能下水。一队亡骑把石船当了马厩，马拴在石桅上，船舱里堆满了干草。几个漂客的老人想进去坐坐，被马踢了出来，他们说这条船「坐着最安心」。

A boat lies on the shore of the coast, built entirely of stone, prow and stern, bulwarks and mast step, nothing missing, except that it can never touch water. A troop of dead riders has made it their stable, horses tied to the stone mast and the hold heaped with hay. A few old castaways who wanted to go in and sit were kicked out by the horses. It's 'the most peaceful boat to sit in', they say.
after: 亡骑退了，老人们坐进石船，舒舒服服地叹了口气。船头刻着「驼客造」。他们说丝路的人一辈子没坐过船，到了海边，见浪就晕，可又说什么也要有条船，就照着一号船的样子拿石头砌了一条：「造在岸上，就不会沉。」他们走的时候，在石船上拜了一拜，像拜一座庙。

The riders withdraw and the old folk settle into the stone boat with contented sighs. Carved on the prow: 'Built by the camel folk.' The Silk Road people had never been on a boat in their lives, they say; they reached the sea and got sick at the sight of a wave, yet they would have a boat no matter what. So they built one of stone after the pattern of Number One. 'Build it on land and it'll never sink.' When they left they bowed in the stone boat as if it were a temple.

name: 转圈湾
Circling Bay
before: 海边一道礁湾，湾里一大群银鱼，几千条，绕着一个圈游，从早游到晚，圈子一丝不乱。一队亡兵站在湾边，跟着鱼群绕着湾走，也是一圈一圈，脚下踩出了一道深沟。漂客们想下网，一靠近，亡兵就把网扯了扔进鱼群里。

A reef-bound bay on the coast holds a great school of silver fish, thousands of them, swimming round and round in a circle from dawn to dusk without the ring ever breaking. A squad of dead soldiers walks the shore with them, round and round as well, until they have worn a deep groove in the ground. Whenever the castaways try to cast a net, the soldiers tear it away and throw it among the fish.
after: 亡兵退了，鱼群还在转。小桨趴在礁上听了一会儿：「它们不是乱转，是在等一个口子。」湾口有一道礁缝，平日太浅，鱼出不去。阿汐算了算日子：再过三天大潮，缝里的水就深了。漂客们说，那年千里号的人也在这儿看过鱼，看了很久，说：「等潮来，它们就走了。我们也是。」

The soldiers withdraw; the fish keep circling. Xiaojiang lies on the reef listening. 'They're not going round aimlessly. They're waiting for a gap.' There is a crack in the reef at the bay's mouth, too shallow most days for the fish to get out. Axi counts the days: three more and the spring tide will deepen it. The Qianli's people watched the fish here too that year, the castaways say, watched them a long time, and said: 'When the tide comes, they'll go. So will we.'

name: 无面营
Faceless Barracks
before: 野地尽头一座大营，营里一排排石屋，石屋前一排排挂着头盔，有的锈得只剩一层皮，有的样式是几百年前的。守墟人最精的一营驻在这里，三路排开，比哪一处都齐整。营门口立着一块黑石碑，碑上只有四个字：「生人勿留」。

At the edge of the open land stands a great camp, row on row of stone huts with row on row of helmets hung before them, some rusted to a skin, some in styles centuries old. The keepers' finest camp is stationed here in three columns, neater than anywhere else. A black stone tablet stands at the gate with only four words on it: 'The living must not stay.'
after: 精兵退了，你们翻过石碑，背面刻着一段古字，墨三一字一字念：「来归墟者，留久则忘其面，忘面者守墟。守墟者驱生人，勿使再忘。」每只头盔里都刻着一个名字，刮得只剩一半：它们也是人，在归墟留得太久，忘了自己长什么样。它们赶人，是不想再有人忘。

The picked guards withdraw and you look at the back of the tablet. An ancient inscription is carved there and Mo San reads it word by word: 'Who comes to the Ruins and stays too long forgets their face. Who forgets their face keeps the Ruins. The keepers drive the living out, that no more may forget.' Inside every helmet a name is scratched, half worn away. They were people too, who stayed in the Ruins too long and forgot what they looked like. They drive people off so no one else will forget.

name: 哑童寨
Silent Child Stockade
before: 海边野地里一座木寨，三路守墟人守得严严实实。寨墙上坐着个八九岁的孩子，光着脚，不说话，看见你们来，朝你们深深弯了个腰，跟拜东坪上守墟人的腰弯得一模一样。守墟人把孩子往身后一挡，枪尖齐齐朝外。

A wooden stockade stands in the open land near the coast, guarded tight by Ruin-keepers in three columns. On top of its wall sits a barefoot child of eight or nine who does not speak. Seeing you come, the child bows to you deeply, exactly the way the keepers bow on the Eastward Bow Flat. The keepers step in front of the child, every spear point turned outward.
after: 守墟人退了，孩子还坐在墙上。漂客们说，他是大浪那年被冲上岸的，爹娘没找着，守墟人把他捡了回去，养在寨里。它们没有脸，教不了他说话，只教会了他弯腰。阿舟爬上墙，在他旁边坐下，掏出海螺吹了一支泉州的南音。孩子听着听着，张开嘴，「啊」了一声。

The keepers withdraw; the child stays on the wall. He was washed ashore the year of the great wave, the castaways say, and no one ever found his parents. The keepers took him in and raised him in the stockade. Having no faces, they couldn't teach him to speak; all they could teach him was to bow. Azhou climbs the wall, sits down beside him and plays a Quanzhou nanyin tune on his conch. The child listens, and listens, then opens his mouth and says, 'Ah.'

name: 封东坡
Walling Slope
before: 野地里一道土坡，坡上的路通往海边。一队亡兵正一块块往路上垒石头，垒成一道墙，墙已经齐胸高了。垒好一层，它们退后看一看，再垒一层。墙那边的漂客要过来，隔着墙喊，亡兵也不理，只管垒。

An earth slope in the open, its road running down to the sea. A squad of dead soldiers is laying stones across the road one by one, building a wall that already stands chest-high. Each time they finish a course they step back, look at it, and lay another. Castaways on the far side want to come through and shout over the wall, but the soldiers pay no heed and keep building.
after: 亡兵退了，你们拆开一个豁口。墙根底下的石头最旧，长了青苔，是十年前垒的：千里号的人从这条路往东去了以后，守墟人就开始垒，白天垒，夜里潮来冲塌一点，第二天接着垒。漂客们说：「它们不是不让人走，是不想再有人从这儿走了回不来。」

The soldiers withdraw and you open a gap. The stones at the base are the oldest, mossy, laid ten years ago: after the Qianli's people went east along this road, the keepers began walling it, building by day while the night tide knocked a little down, and building again the next morning. 'They're not trying to stop people leaving,' the castaways say. 'They just don't want anyone else to go this way and never come back.'

name: 借火亭
Borrowed Fire Pavilion
before: 野地里一座小亭，亭里一盏灯，灯罩熏得发黑，火苗不大，十年没灭过。附近的漂客要生火，都来这儿借，点一根草棍带回去。一队亡骑围着小亭打转，守墟人见不得火，拿马蹄刨沙往灯上扬，扬一回，借火的人就扑上去用身子挡一回。

A little pavilion in the open with a single lamp inside, its chimney smoked black, its flame small, and it has not gone out in ten years. When castaways nearby need to light a fire, they come here to borrow, kindling a stalk of grass to carry home. A troop of dead riders circles the pavilion, for the keepers cannot abide fire, kicking sand at the lamp with their hooves, and each time the borrowers throw themselves in the way.
after: 亡骑散了，灯还亮着。灯座上刻着一行小字：「此灯不在数内。」漂客们说，东边那片灯是一盏一盏点起来的，点到最后，这一盏点好了，却没有搬过去，就放在了这儿。「点灯的人说，这一盏是给路上的，谁路过，谁借个火。」

The riders scatter, and the lamp still burns. A line is cut into its base: 'This lamp is not counted.' The lights to the east were lit one at a time, the castaways say, and when the last of them was done, this one was lit too but never carried over; it was set down here instead. 'The lamplighter said this one is for the road. Whoever passes can borrow a light.'

name: 灯前坂
Lamp Front Slope
before: 往东最后一道坡，坡顶就能看见那片灯了：一盏一盏摆在一片平地上，排成一行行，静得像星星落了一地。坡上驻着一营守墟人，三路排开，枪尖朝西，背对着灯。它们站得笔直，像守了很多年的城门。沈渡站在你们中间，把那本账抱紧了。

The last slope on the way east, and from its crest you can see the lamps at last: set out one by one across a level field in row after row, as still as if the stars had fallen to the ground. A camp of Ruin-keepers holds the slope in three columns, spears pointing west, backs to the lamps, standing ramrod straight like the guard of a city gate kept for many years. Shen Du stands among you, holding her ledger tight.
after: 守墟人退下坡去，在两边排成行，弯下了腰，像拜东坪上那样。墨三举着灯笼数了三遍：二百九十九盏，一盏不多，一盏不少。灯阵当中有一张矮桌，桌后坐着一个人，戴着斗笠，背对着你们，正拿一根细竹签，一盏一盏地挑灯芯。

The keepers withdraw down the slope, form ranks on either side, and bend low as they do on the Eastward Bow Flat. Mo San holds up a lantern and counts three times: two hundred and ninety-nine lamps, not one more, not one fewer. In the middle of them stands a low table, and behind it sits a figure in a straw hat with his back to you, trimming the wicks one by one with a thin bamboo pick.
